title: Four characterisations of an identity system over a pointed type are logically equivalent
author: The Univalent Foundations Program
work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file induction.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled theorem at source lines 1152-1160 (book Theorem 5.8.2): four conditions on a pointed predicate over a pointed type, namely being an identity system, having a contractible type of pointed maps into every pointed predicate, having all the transport maps out of the loop space be equivalences, and having a contractible total type, are logically equivalent. The statement lists the four conditions and nothing else, while the proof (source lines 1167-1193) runs the cycle in one direction only and must construct, for each implication, the auxiliary pointed predicate and the two pointed maps that make the argument go through: for the first implication it turns the identity-system elimination into inhabitation and then into a mere proposition by applying elimination to the equality of any two pointed maps; for the second it uses (a_0 = b) as the auxiliary family and gets the composites to be identities from the contractibility of the pointed-map types ppmap(R,R) and ppmap(S,S); the third goes through the equivalence of \Sigma-types; the fourth has to transport the given element along a uniform path family of the contractible total type and check the base-point computation. Only the derived direction of each implication is proved, so the chapter's observation that the four conditions are also logically equivalent as propositions is used, not proved.
